title: Add automated Postgres Raft recovery playbooks and Terraform rollback steps
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Added automated runbooks-as-code for Postgres Raft cluster restore and failover; Terraform rollback helpers and Helm hooks for lifecycle orchestration. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Summary: Adds a set of automated recovery playbooks (as Helm hooks + Ansible-friendly tasks) and Terraform rollback helpers to accelerate Postgres Raft cluster restore and controlled failover in private deployments. Motivation: during recent DR rehearsals we spent significant manual time rebuilding quorum and replaying WAL; this set codifies those steps so on-call can execute a safe, repeatable restore with clear guardrails.

What this PR contains: commits, high-level diffs, and review notes compressed into a single narrative.

Motivation and goals: Ensure private (VPC/on-prem) customers using the integrated Postgres Raft operator can: 1) perform automated partial-restore to rejoin a minority/isolated AZ, 2) failover leadership in a controlled manner when quorum is lost, 3) run a 'preflight' validation that verifies WAL continuity and S3 snapshot availability before touchpoints, and 4) rollback Terraform state to the most recent validated checkpoint in case of botched upgrades. This is focused on operational run-time safety, not changes to the runtime code path.

High-level changes: - pkg/installer/helm/hooks/pg-recovery-hook.yaml: new Helm pre-delete and post-upgrade hooks that wrap operator-managed drain and snapshot steps. - terraform/modules/postgres/rollback-helper.tf: helper module to register and apply a state-safe rollback (uses remote state lock and snapshot tags). - playbooks/dr/pg-raft-recover.yml: opinionated, idempotent playbook that orchestrates snapshot restore, wal replay, and leader-election fencing. - docs/runbooks/pg-raft-recovery.md: runbook-as-code with step-by-step checks, expected outputs and emergency abort procedures. - tests/fixtures/pg-recover-scenario.sh: small harness to exercise the playbook against a local minikube/postgres-raft replica set.

Commits (summary): 1) 9f2b3c: scaffold playbook and docs; 2) 5a7d1e: terraform rollback helper and examples; 3) d4e1b7: helm hook templates + lifecycle hooks; 4) b29011: tests and CI matrix; 5) 2f8c90: address reviewer feedback and tighten idempotency checks.

Selected diffs (illustrative snippets only): - playbooks/dr/pg-raft-recover.yml (new): task: - name: "Validate latest snapshot" shell: "aws s3api head-object --bucket {{ snapshots_bucket }} --key {{ snapshot_key }}" register: snap_ok changed_when: false failed_when: snap_ok.rc != 0
- terraform/modules/postgres/rollback-helper.tf (new): resource "null_resource" "apply_rollback" { provisioner "local-exec" { command = "./scripts/rollback-to-tag.sh ${var.tag} || exit 1" } triggers = { tag = var.tag } }
- helm/hooks/pg-recovery-hook.yaml (new): apiVersion: batch/v1 jobTemplate: spec: template: spec: containers: - name: preflight-checks image: {{ .Values.recovery.image }} command: ["/bin/recovery", "--preflight"]

Testing and CI: - Added a new CI matrix entry (tests:pg_recovery) that runs the playbook against a lightweight kind cluster and a mocked S3 backend. - Full pipeline status on merge: linux-lint: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass, tests:pg_recovery: pass, terraform-check: pass, helm-lint: pass. No flaky tests observed during re-runs.

Security and risk review: No secrets are checked in. The Terraform helpers use remote state and require a pre-existing snapshot tag to run; we added guardrails that block automatic rollback if the tag is older than 72 hours without an explicit override. RBAC: the Helm hooks run as a ServiceAccount bound to a cluster-admin-like role in private deployments by default; reviewers asked for least-privilege guidance, and docs now include a minimal role binding template.

Operational runbook highlights (excerpts): - Preflight: run ./scripts/preflight-check.sh --cluster $CLUSTER --snapshot-tag $TAG -> expects OK for WAL continuity and snapshot presence. - Dry-run restore: ansible-playbook playbooks/dr/pg-raft-recover.yml -e "state=dry_run" - This will not change StatefulSets or PVCs but will verify replay steps. - Controlled failover: annotate the leader Pod with redwood-internal/recovery=force-failover then execute the playbook with state=apply. - Rollback terraform: terraform workspace select production && terraform apply -var="rollback_tag=$TAG" - A manual approve is required by the helper script.

Review conversation (recreated): - Lena Park (review): "Overall this is a big win for on-call. Two requests: make the helm hook timeouts configurable and ensure the hook gracefully handles API rate limits when checking S3." - Priya (author): "Added adjustable timeouts and exponential backoff helper in recovery container image; updated docs to call out ENV vars RECOVERY_TIMEOUT and BACKOFF_RETRIES." - Miguel Santos (review): "Please add a safety gate so terraform rollback cannot be applied without a signed oncall_ack in SSM parameter store." - Priya: "Added parameter gating and documented the SSM pattern. The helper now refuses to run if oncall_ack is not present." - Ava Thompson (approval): "Verified local dry-run and helm-lint; approving pending CI green." - CI run: green, no required changes.

Edge cases considered: - Split-brain: playbook will check for majority reachable nodes and refuse automated apply if another majority exists in a conflicting state. - WAL gaps: if replay fails due to missing WAL, the playbook surfaces a clear diagnostic and a next-step recommendation (manual WAL fetch or failover). - Storage portability: supports both S3-compatible backends and on-prem NFS snapshots; detection logic picks correct verifier.

Backward compatibility and upgrade notes: There are no schema changes to operator CRDs in this PR. Helm hooks are optional and gated behind values.recovery.enabled=false by default, so existing installs are unaffected until operators enable the feature.

Merge details: merged via squash-merge after CI passed and three reviewers approved. Release note entry created in docs/releases/2025-11.md.

Follow-ups tracked: - ENG-1886: add metrics and tracing spans for recovery runs (observability). - OPS-1010: schedule quarterly automated rehearsal job. - ENG-1903: convert playbook harness to a fully mocked unit test in the eval-harness repo.

If you want to run the new flow locally: 1) export KUBECONFIG pointing to a kind cluster; 2) export SNAPSHOT_BUCKET=redwood-test-snaps; 3) make test-pg-recovery; 4) run ansible-playbook playbooks/dr/pg-raft-recover.yml -e 'state=dry_run'.

Contact: Priya Menon (author) for follow-up and debug tips.
